Ethanol in a decomposed body: drunk before death or made after

Source: R/tox.R
etohlr.Rd

Microbes make ethanol in a body after death, and with it the higher alcohols n-propanol and n-butanol; ethyl glucuronide, a metabolite, is made only by a living body. So for each case: ethyl glucuronide present (above 0) says the ethanol was taken before death; otherwise a higher alcohol above thr says it was (at least partly) made after death; otherwise the signals do not decide.

Usage

etohlr(eth, prop = 0, but = 0, etg = NA, thr = 0)

Arguments

eth

The ethanol concentration: numbers from 0, one per case.

prop, but

The n-propanol and n-butanol concentrations: numbers or NA (not measured), one per case or one for all.

etg

The ethyl glucuronide concentration: numbers or NA (not measured), one per case or one for all.

thr

The level a higher alcohol must exceed: one number from 0.

Value

A data frame with one row per case: eth, prop, but, etg, higher (the larger higher alcohol, NA when neither was measured) and verdict, a factor (antemortem, postmortem, indeterminate).

References

Kugelberg, F. C. and Jones, A. W. (2007). Interpreting results of ethanol analysis in postmortem specimens: a review of the literature. Forensic Science International, 165(1), 10-29. doi:10.1016/j.forsciint.2006.05.004

Examples

etohlr(c(0.8, 0.5, 0.3), prop = c(0, 0.02, NA), etg = c(1.1, NA, NA))
#>   eth prop but etg higher       verdict
#> 1 0.8 0.00   0 1.1   0.00    antemortem
#> 2 0.5 0.02   0  NA   0.02    postmortem
#> 3 0.3   NA   0  NA   0.00 indeterminate
